explanation: At the station's height, gravity is still about 90% as strong as on the ground. The crew and station fall around Earth together, so nothing presses them to the floor.

claims.text: Astronauts float on the ISS because they and the station are in continuous free fall around Earth.
At the ISS's orbital height gravity is about 90% as strong as at Earth's surface, so it is false that space there has no gravity or that Earth's pull is too weak.
Air pressure inside the station does not lift the astronauts.
Because the crew and the station fall together, nothing presses the crew against the floor.
